newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MUSSINA FLIRTS WITH NO-HITTER AGAIN, O'S BOMB BREWERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MUSSINA FLIRTS WITH NO-HITTER AGAIN, O'S BOMB BREWERS.

text.p: Mike Mussina flirted with a no-hitter for the second time this season and Jeffrey Hammonds hit a pair of two-run homers as the Baltimore Orioles rolled to a 9-1 victory over the Brewers Wednesday.

Mussina (9-2) did not allow a hit until the eighth inning, when he surrendered a clean leadoff single by Jose Valentin into right field. He lost his shutout bid with two out in the ninth on a sacrifice fly by Dave Nilsson.
Mussina, who carried a perfect game into the ninth inning of a shutout of the Indians on May 30, struck out a season-high 12 batters and walked one.
"I kind of had the same feeling I had the other day," said Mussina. "Sooner or later, somebody is going to get a hit. This is the major leagues and that happens. I just kept on going out there.
"But I thought about it a little bit."
"Moose was special," said Orioles manager Davey Johnson.
"He was on the corners all day, mixed his pitches up well and kept the ball down. It was fun to watch."
Baltimore became the first team to reach the 50-win mark in baseball this year and Mussina improved to 5-1 all-time against the Brewers.
Hammonds hit two-run homers in the second and third innings. Ex-Brewer B.J. Surhoff added a two-run shot and Dave Dellucci got his first major-league homer, a solo blast.
Cal Eldred (7-8) was rocked for six runs and seven hits in three innings, the shortest outing of his career and the shortest by a Milwaukee starter this season.

In Toronto, red-hot Nomar Garciaparra went 3-for-4 and scored twice and was one of five players to homer off Pat Hentgen as the Boston Red Sox outslugged the Blue Jays 13-12, handing the Jays their season-high fifth straight loss.

Garciaparra, who tied career highs with four hits and four runs in Tuesday's 9-6 win, hit the first pitch of the game for his 12th homer of the season. Reggie Jefferson, Mike Stanley, Darren Bragg and Troy O'Leary also homered off Hentgen (8-4), the 1996 Cy Young Award winner.
John Valentin tripled, doubled, hit a sacrifice fly and extended his hitting streak to 10 games for the Red Sox, who won their fourth straight.
Boston has won 14 of its last 19 games in Toronto and jumped ahead of the Blue Jays in the American League Eastern Division standings.

Tim Wakefield (3-7) got the win despite allowing six runs and four hits over 5 2/3 innings. Heathcliff Slocumb notched his fourth save in as many days and 10th of the season by getting the final out with the bases loaded.
In Seattle, Edgar Martinez hit a pair of solo homers and Paul Sorrento added a three-run shot to lead the Mariners to a 9-4 rout over the Oakland Athletics.
Bob Wolcott (4-4) allowed two runs and nine hits over 7 2/3 innings. Oakland starter Don Wengert (3-6) took the loss.

Seattle's Ken Griffey Jr, the major league leader in home runs with 29, left the game in the bottom of the first after suffering tightness in his right hamstring running out a double. He was to be re-evaluated on Thursday.
For Oakland, Rafael Bournigal went 4-for-4, including a his first career homer, a two-run shot.
At Texas, Mark McLemore's one-out single in the bottom of the ninth scored the winning run as the Rangers snapped a seven-game losing streak, 5-4 over the Anaheim Angels.
Mike Holtz (2-2) took the loss after throwing wildly on a come-backer by Mickey Tettleton. Benji Gil pinch-ran for Tettleton and eventually scored the game-winner.
Eric Gunderson (1-0) pitched a hitless ninth for Texas.
Anaheim had a six-game winning streak snapped.
In Detroit, Charlie Hayes hit a two-run homer in the ninth to break a tie as the New York Yankees beat the Tigers 3-1 for a sweep of their three-game series.
Tino Martinez hit his 26th homer for the Yankees. He was 8-for-12 with four homers and six RBI in the series.

Mike Stanton (4-0) pitched a scoreless eighth for the win and Mariano Rivera pitched the ninth for his 25th save, tying Rod Beck of San Francisco and Randy Myers of Baltimore for the major league lead. Rivera had saves in each of the three wins over the Tigers. Justin Thompson (7-6) took the loss.
In Chicago, rookie pinch-hitter Mario Valdez blooped a two-out single in the bottom of the 10th to score Albert Belle as the White Sox rallyed for an 8-7 victory over the Kansas City Royals.
Harold Baines hit a three-run homer in the eighth to tie the game. He also tied Hank Greenberg for 58th place on the all-time list with his 331st career homer. Mike Cameron also homered for Chicago.
The Cleveland game between the Minnesota Twins and the Indians was postponed due to rain. No reschedule date was announced.
